1. Key local requirements wrongly say association needs 3+ founders: Law on Associations and Foundations Art. 15 requires at least 5 founders, 3 of whom must have domicile/residence (or seat) in North Macedonia. 2. Foundation requires minimum endowment of EUR 10,000, which should be stated.

1. Membership associations require at least 5 natural persons or 2 legal persons as founders (Law 8788/2001 Art. 10), not 3. 2. Under Law 80/2021 the NPO register is kept by the Tirana court (Tirana Judicial District Court, now Court of First Instance of General Jurisdiction Tirana), not the National Registration Center; Constitutional Court decision of 20.11.2023 partially struck down parts of Law 80/2021.

1. Under Law 86/2020 a public association can be founded by 2 or more persons (natural or legal), not 3+. 2. Registration by the Public Services Agency is free for non-commercial organisations and the statutory term is 15 days.

1. State registration of a public association (Law 'On Public Associations' 4572-VI) is free of charge; there is no ~2,000 UAH (~$50) state duty; statutory review is ~3 working days. 2. 'fundatsiia' is not a distinct form; the charitable-foundation form is blagodiinyi fond under the Law on Charitable Activities and Charitable Organizations (5073-VI, 2012). 3. Foreign individual founders must be lawfully staying in Ukraine.

1. Under NPLE Act Art. 19 an association needs at least 3 founders (7 natural or 3 legal persons for public-benefit), not 5; a foundation can have 1 founder. 2. Registry Agency registration fee is about BGN 50 (~EUR 25, ~$30), not $75-150; Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 Jan 2026 so fees are now in EUR.

1. A Greek association (somateio) requires at least 20 founding members (Civil Code Art. 78), not 7 or 5. 2. Law 5259/2025 (FEK A 228/12.12.2025) repealed Law 4182/2013 for public-benefit foundations; the '2019 law' reference in Notes is unsupported. 3. Since the 2016 Civil Procedure reform, association registration is ordered by the Magistrates' Court (Eirinodikeio), not the first-instance court. 4. Fee column (~$1,300) is mostly notary/legal cost, not a government fee.

1. A society under the Societies and Institutions Law 104(I)/2017 requires at least 20 founding persons (not 3 or 7); an institution (idryma) may have one founder. Registration is with the District Officer/Registrar, who has up to 3 months to examine a complete application, so 2-6 weeks is optimistic. 2. A company limited by guarantee with a Council of Ministers licence under the Companies Law Cap. 113 (s.20) is the usual alternative, not s.250.

Companies Act 2014 s.137 requires at least one EEA-resident (not EU) director, or a EUR 25,000 s.137 bond / s.140 certificate instead.

Registration with the Charity Commission is only required (and possible) for charities with income over GBP 5,000, except CIOs which register at any income.

1. Act 33/1999 covers foundations engaged in business operations; non-business charitable foundations fall under Act 19/1988 (funds/institutions with approved charters, charter approved by the District Commissioner/Syslumadur, indexed minimum capital, amended by Act 112/2024). 2. Associations/public-benefit organisations are governed by Act 110/2021 on third-sector organisations; tax-deductible status comes via registration on Skatturinn's public-benefit register (almannaheillaskra, Acts 32/2021 and 133/2021), not a 'reykjafrjalsefni' exemption; RSK is now called Skatturinn.

1. Altinn states an association needs at least 2 founders (not 3). 2. Foundations Act (stiftelsesloven) minimum capital is NOK 100,000 for ordinary foundations (NOK 200,000 commercial), not ~NOK 1m; foundation registration carries a fee (~NOK 2,656 electronic) unlike associations.
